identity.title: Outflows, cores, and magnetic field orientations in W43-MM1 as seen by ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present five pointings with ALMA in full polarization targeting the most massive dense cores in W43-MM1

evidence.quote: W43-MM1, which is at a distance of 5.5 kpc from the Sun (cite: zhangb+14)

question.value: Is the core-scale magnetic field orientation correlated with the orientation of dense cores and protostellar outflows in W43-MM1?

evidence.quote: We aim to reveal any correlation between the magnetic field orientation and the orientation of the cores and outflows in a sample of protostellar dense cores in the W43-MM1 high-mass star-forming region.
We used the Atacama Large Millimeter Array in Band 6 (1.3 mm) in full polarization mode
four spectral windows centered at 224.984, 226.984, 239.015, and 241.015 GHz
Each spectral window has 64 channels of 31.250 MHz each
corresponding to a total bandwidth of 1.875 GHz per spectral window
The ALMA observations were obtained between April and May 2016 using an array with 35 antennas.
with an angular resolution of 0.55$^{''}$ $\times$ 0.49$^{''}$
The maximum recoverable scale is $\sim$10.6$^{''}$.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive debiased polarized intensity and B-field angles

method.value: P=sqrt(Q^2+U^2), Vaillancourt debiasing, 3 sigma_P threshold, chi=0.5 arctan(U/Q), rotate 90 deg

evidence.quote: We wielded the 3$\sigma_{\mathrm{P}}$ debiased intensity value as a threshold to select the pixels used to derive the polarization angle maps

assumptions.value: Grain alignment by radiative alignment torques; polarization perpendicular to B

evidence.quote: we assumed alignment of the grains with respect to the magnetic field due to the "radiative alignment torques" mechanism (RATs)

method.value: Average Q and U within each core area (2D Gaussian of Stokes I), only within one-third of primary beam; error propagation

evidence.quote: where *Q* and *U* are the mean Stokes $Q$ and $U$ intensities averaged within each core, whose area is defined by a 2D Gaussian fit of its Stokes $I$ emission.

key_parameters.value: within one-third of primary beam; 52 cores, 29 with polarization

findings_qualitative.value: Core orientation is not random with respect to B; compatible with 20-50 deg

evidence.quote: the dense cores are compatible with being oriented 20-50$^\circ$ with respect to the magnetic field.

claims.hypothesis: Cores are randomly oriented relative to B
claims.experiment: KS tests of core PA minus B-field PA vs synthetic populations
claims.result: Only the 20-50 deg population is not rejected (p=0.76)
claims.finding: Cores are nonrandomly oriented, 20-50 deg to B, contradicting magnetically controlled collapse models

evidence.quote: All of the synthetic populations (including the random distribution), except for the 20-50$^\circ$ distribution, are rejected by the KS test.

claims.experiment: KS tests on outflow minus B-field angles
claims.result: Parallel and perpendicular rejected; random or 50-70 deg allowed
claims.finding: Outflows are either random or 50-70 deg to B; cannot discriminate

evidence.quote: Given our statistics, we could not discriminate between these two possibilities.

why_this_method.value: KS test chosen over chi-squared because preferable for nonequally sampled data

evidence.quote: We chose the KS test over the chi-squared test as the former is preferable to compare nonequally sampled data.

limitations_admitted.value: Sample size does not allow discriminating 50-70 deg, random, or bimodal populations

evidence.quote: it is not statistically possible to discriminate between the 50-70$^\circ$ orientation, a random orientation, or an 85% random population plus a 15% orthogonal population.

referee_caveats_inferred: Small samples; KS p-values depend on projection assumptions
Core elongation as disk proxy is assumed
Core PA errors treat only measurement error
Spatial correlation of cores not accounted for
